blocks.text: Condo buildings in Downtown Vancouver

Every first-page card is labelled with the board sub-area "Downtown VW" and a Vancouver mailing address, on streets including Hornby Street, Howe Street, West Pender Street, Seymour Street, Pacific Street, Burrard Street, Homer Street and Keefer Place. The City of Vancouver has only ONE Downtown local area, one of its 22 distinct areas; "VW" is a board/site distinction, not a City one, and Coal Harbour and Yaletown are their own board sub-areas inside/beside that local area, while the West End is a separate official local area.
Streets, schools and transit near Downtown Vancouver condos

items.t: Where the condo stock concentrates: almost entirely strata apartment form in towers above and beside the business district — the City describes Downtown as the primary business district, and the Downtown District (DD) schedule permits residential uses within a district whose permitted uses are commercial, residential, institutional, light industrial, parks and open spaces, and public uses; detached houses are not a downtown housing form.

Health care: St. Paul's Hospital, 1081 Burrard Street, is inside the Downtown local area on the Burrard corridor; it is a Providence Health Care hospital, not a VCH site. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is in Fairview.
Library: Vancouver Public Library Central Library, 350 West Georgia Street, is in the downtown core.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station, running to SFU Exchange via Hastings Street; route 50 starts at Waterfront Station and runs via Chinatown, Granville Island and the False Creek south shore to Olympic Village Station; route 22 runs from Burrard Station via Pender, Gore, Prior, Venables, Clark and Knight; Yaletown–Roundhouse Station on the Canada Line serves the area's south side, between Vancouver City Centre and Olympic Village Stations.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Downtown Vancouver

items.t: Vancouver property taxes: City of Vancouver 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes were due July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after each due date; the home owner grant was also due July 3, 2026.

Empty Homes Tax (Vancouver): the Empty Homes Tax applies in the City of Vancouver — every owner must submit an annual property status declaration (due February 3, 2026), and properties declared, determined or deemed empty in the 2025 reference year are taxed at 3% of the property's 2025 assessed taxable value; the 2025 Empty Homes Tax payment was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after that date. The Province's Speculation and Vacancy Tax is separate and in addition.

Additional school tax: the Province's additional school tax can apply at downtown price points — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Downtown Vancouver condos

items.t: Downtown has elementaries but no confirmed secondary. Elsie Roy and šxʷməqʷəθət Crosstown elementaries are listed under Downtown; King George Secondary (1755 Barclay St) is in the West End, and no public secondary inside the Downtown local area was confirmed — a family buying downtown is buying an elementary catchment question, not a settled secondary.

There is no downtown median to quote, from any permitted source. SnapStats publishes no Vancouver figures at all, so any "downtown Vancouver median condo price" a buyer is quoted from that source does not exist.

Fee-simple lots, bare-land strata, leasehold

items.t: Fee-simple house lots: none exist to document: There is no historic house-lot fabric downtown — the peninsula's lot fabric is commercial and strata parcels under DD/CD-1/C-3A.
Downtown condo tenure varies by building (freehold strata and leasehold both exist in the wider downtown stock's framing).
Serviced position: downtown stock is fully urban serviced stock on City water and sewer.
Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals
Downtown presale history sells strata units and airspace parcels, not lots.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Downtown Vancouver lots

items.t: What the page covers: the downtown-wide condos band for the City of Vancouver's official local area "Downtown," on the board's Vancouver West (VW) side — every first-page card is labelled "Downtown VW" with a Vancouver mailing address, on streets including Hornby Street, Howe Street, West Pender Street, Seymour Street, Pacific Street, Burrard Street, Homer Street and Keefer Place. It is not the Yaletown-only page and not a detached-house page.

One City area, board slices: the City of Vancouver has only ONE Downtown local area, one of its 22 distinct areas; "VW" is a board/site distinction, not a City one. Coal Harbour and Yaletown are their own board sub-areas inside/beside that local area, and the West End is a separate official local area.

Zoning frame: the Downtown District (DD) schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 governs much of the core — permitted uses are those in the Downtown District Official Development Plan (commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and open spaces, and public uses); CD-1 and C-3A districts also apply in parts of the area.

Heritage: Yaletown, at the area's south side, is a City protected heritage area (HA-3), bordered by Homer and Nelson streets to the north and east, and Cambie, Mainland and Drake streets to the south and west.
Schools (SD39, Ministry-listed names only): Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake St, and šxʷməqʷəθət Crosstown Elementary, 55 Expo Blvd — both listed by the VSB under Downtown.

Civic anchors: Vancouver Public Library Central Library, 350 West Georgia Street, is in the downtown core; St. Paul's Hospital, 1081 Burrard Street, is inside the Downtown local area (a Providence Health Care hospital). Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is in Fairview.
Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at Burrard Station; route 22 runs from Burrard Station; Yaletown–Roundhouse Station on the Canada Line serves the area's south side.
Market numbers: none.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Downtown Vancouver

items.t: Zoning framework: DD schedule of By-law No. 3575 (uses per the Downtown District Official Development Plan), plus site-specific CD-1 districts and C-3A districts in parts of the area — there is no house-lot minimum table to quote; the parcel's own district governs.
SSMUH position: Density is set by the DD/CD-1 position of the specific parcel.

Heritage controls: the City's heritage areas carry regulations for Gastown, Chinatown and Yaletown that preserve and protect historic fabric and affect renovation, alteration and any redevelopment of a heritage-district parcel from day one.

Floodplain diligence: the City's designated floodplain includes the False Creek coastal floodplain, and land in it is subject to the Vancouver Building By-law Floodplain Standards and Requirements for shoreline setbacks and flood construction levels.

Strata diligence — the operative regime downtown (the BC strata block): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page) — read it with the depreciation report, contingency reserve and any special levies before pricing an offer; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw, and Vancouver licences short-term rentals); only 55+ age bylaws valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw. This same block would apply in full to any bare-land strata lot, if one existed here.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

Empty Homes Tax — vancouver only, applies here, rate 3%: the City's Empty Homes Tax is 3% of assessed value for vacant properties; every Vancouver owner must submit an annual property status declaration (due February 3, 2026's reading), and the 2025 Empty Homes Tax payment was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance after that date.

Additional school tax: 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Downtown Vancouver lots

items.t: Downtown's "land" fee line is the airspace line: Vancouver's 2026 subdivision Schedule F prices a downtown-scale proposal as Class V (Air Space) at $125,100 where FSR exceeds 3.0 — there is no lot-split fee a downtown buyer will ever pay, because there are no lots to split.

The additional school tax steps up on a fixed date: the rates that apply at downtown price points (0.2% / 0.4%) rise to 0.3% / 0.6% on January 1, 2027 — a closing that straddles that date carries two different tax years' math on the same assessment.

faq.q: Can I rent out a downtown condo long-term, and can I run it as an Airbnb?
faq.a: Long-term: yes in law — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC.

faq.q: What extra tax hits a high-end downtown purchase?
faq.a: Beyond PTT, the Province's additional school tax applies on the residential portion of assessed value above $3 million — 0.2% between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

faq.q: Is Downtown VW a different neighbourhood from Yaletown or the West End?
faq.a: The City of Vancouver has one Downtown local area; Yaletown sits within it but is its own board sub-area with its own page, Coal Harbour is its own board sub-area, and the West End is a separate City local area. And "Downtown West Vancouver" is simply wrong — West Vancouver is a different municipality.

faq.q: Can I rent out a downtown unit long-term, or run it as an Airbnb?
faq.a: Long-term: yes in law — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot or a house lot downtown?
faq.a: What exists is strata apartment product, rental buildings, and parcel-level development rights under DD/CD-1 zoning.
No. This is Downtown VANCOUVER, on the downtown peninsula in the City of Vancouver; West Vancouver is a separate municipality across Burrard Inlet with its own bylaws, taxes and market.

faq.q: What zoning governs a downtown parcel?
faq.a: Most of the core sits under the Downtown District (DD) schedule of By-law No. 3575, which permits the uses in the Downtown District Official Development Plan — commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and open spaces, and public uses — with CD-1 site-specific districts and C-3A districts in parts of the area. There is no house-lot minimum table to quote.

faq.q: When are property taxes due on a downtown Vancouver condo?
faq.a: To the City of Vancouver: advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes were due July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid balances after each due date, and every owner must also file the annual Empty Homes Tax property status declaration (due February 3, 2026).
St. Paul's Hospital, 1081 Burrard Street, on the Burrard corridor — a Providence Health Care hospital. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is in Fairview, south across False Creek.
